newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks drop on finance, export worries.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks drop on finance, export worries.

text.p: The Thai stock market dipped slightly on Wednesday as investors sold some large capitalised stocks on concern over weak first quarter finance company results and continued declines in exports, brokers said.

"Market sentiment was poor due to persistent worries by investors over poor first quarter earnings of finance companies. Comments on exports later in the afternoon also weakened the market," said Payuha Boonsiri of Nithipat Capital.
The composite SET index declined 1.37 points to 689.79 on thin 2.3 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index fell 0.21 point to 52.12.
Decliners led gainers 143 to 116 while 107 issues remained unchanged.
Thai Deputy Finance Minister Thawatwongse Na Chiang Mai said before the market reopened in the afternoon that the country's exports in February contracted by five percent year-on-year.
He attributed the negative export trend to the strengthening of the Thai baht against the yen and the German mark.
Brokers said the market remained sluggish as investors opted to wait for the official release of monthly key economic indicators by the central bank on Thursday.
"Investment in the stock market would rise if investors see an improvement in the country's exports. Right now the market lacks positive factors to induce investors to enter the market," Payuha said.
The banking sector was most active in terms of value, rising 0.11 percent. The communication sector dropped 0.46 percent and the finance sector retreated 0.90 percent.
Shinawatra Computer topped the active list, unchanged at 204 baht. Krung Thai Bank declined 0.50 to 35.50 and United Communication fell five to 164.
